summary: Defines a Type-Length-Value format for Cryptographically Generated Address extensions and updates RFC 3972. This provides a flexible way to add extra data into a CGA's parameters. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines a standard layout for extra data in Cryptographically Generated Address parameters. Each item identifies its type, gives its length and then carries its data.

questions: what is the cga extension field format
subtitle: A Type-Length-Value format for Cryptographically Generated Address extensions.

tldr.problem: CGA extension fields can carry extra information, but multiple data items need a shared format.
tldr.mechanism: Each extension uses a 16-bit type, a 16-bit data length in octets and variable-length data.
tldr.outcome: The RFC updates RFC 3972 and establishes an IANA registry for CGA extension types.

today: RFC 4581 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3972. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 4581.

sections.title: Why Extension Fields Need a Format
sections.content:
The Cryptographically Generated Address specification, RFC 3972, defines extension fields for adding information to a CGA Parameter Data Structure. The authors expected that more than one mechanism might use these fields.

This RFC updates RFC 3972 and defines a Type-Length-Value (TLV) format to make it simpler to include multiple data items.
sections.plainLanguage: Several mechanisms may add information to a CGA. This format gives each added item the same basic structure.

sections.title: The Extension Field Layout
sections.content: Data items in extension fields MUST use three parts. A 16-bit Extension Type identifies the kind of field. A 16-bit unsigned Extension Data Length gives the data length in octets. The remaining Extension Data is variable in length and has meaning specific to its type.
sections.plainLanguage: Each extension starts with a type and a length. The bytes after them hold the data for that type.

sections.title: The CGA Extension Type Registry
sections.content:
IANA maintains a registry called CGA Extension Type. Its values are 16-bit unsigned integers, and future assignments require Standards Action.

For experimental and testing use, the RFC assigns 0xFFFD as Exp_FFFD, 0xFFFE as Exp_FFFE and 0xFFFF as Exp_FFFF.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA keeps the list of extension types. The RFC sets aside three type values for experiments and testing.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says adopting the extension format raises no security concerns by itself. It also says each new CGA extension needs proper security analysis to check that it introduces no new vulnerabilities to existing CGA schemes.
sections.plainLanguage: The shared layout raises no security concern on its own. Each new kind of extension still needs its own security analysis.

fields.name: Extension Data Length
fields.desc: Length of the data in octets.
